sections.title: Basic Concept of Column Matching
sections.content: In Column Matching questions, two columns are provided. Column 1 contains the first part of a sentence and Column 2 contains its possible endings. The objective is to match them so that a grammatically correct and meaningful sentence is formed.

sections.title: Basic Subject-Verb Agreement
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the subject. Step 2: Check whether the subject is singular or plural. Step 3: Match it with the correct verb option accordingly. Example: 'The boy' should be matched with 'plays in the park' because a singular subject takes a singular verb.

sections.title: Simple Prepositions
sections.content: Step 1: Identify whether the sentence refers to place or time. Step 2: Choose the correct preposition such as in, on, or at. Step 3: Match it with the correct phrase. Example: 'She lives' should be matched with 'in Delhi'.

sections.title: Logical Completion of Sentences
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the meaning of the first part of the sentence. Step 2: Read the options in Column 2. Step 3: Match the option that logically completes the sentence. Example: 'The teacher explained the lesson' can be matched with 'to the students clearly'.

sections.title: Matching Strategy
sections.content: Step 1: Check grammar first. Step 2: Then verify whether the meaning is logical. Step 3: The pair that forms a correct and natural sentence will be the right answer.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Matching based only on meaning while ignoring grammar. 2. Not paying attention to subject-verb agreement. 3. Choosing incorrect prepositions.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Column Matching, both grammar and meaning are important. The correct pair is chosen by considering subject-verb agreement, proper prepositions, and logical sentence construction.

tricks.title: Identify the Subject First
tricks.explanation: Identify the subject in the first part of the sentence and then choose the verb phrase accordingly.

tricks.title: Verb Form Check
tricks.explanation: Match singular subjects with singular verbs and plural subjects with plural verbs.
tricks.example: The boys → are playing in the field.

tricks.title: Preposition Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Recognize common prepositions such as in/at for place and on for days.

tricks.title: Meaning Match Rule
tricks.explanation: Read both columns together and check whether the sentence sounds natural.
tricks.example: She bought a book → from the market.

tricks.title: Daily Life Logic
tricks.explanation: Use common real-life understanding to judge the meaning of the sentence.

tricks.title: Quick Elimination
tricks.explanation: First eliminate options that are grammatically incorrect or meaningless.
tricks.example: The sun rises → in the east.

tricks.title: Read Full Sentence
tricks.explanation: Combine both parts and read the full sentence to ensure it flows naturally.
tricks.example: The children are playing → in the park.

tricks.title: Check Time and Place
tricks.explanation: If the sentence refers to time or place, match it with the correct phrase.
